title: What Do Multilingual Self-Supervised Speech Encoders Know About Sentence Meaning?
abstract: arXiv:2611.17686v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Self-supervised speech models (S3Ms) have been scaled up to thousands of languages and millions of hours of audio, yet little is known about how these models structure semantic knowledge across languages. In this work, we probe sentence-level semantics in massively multilingual S3Ms across 76 languages, using linear maps from frozen speech representations into a frozen text embedding space, evaluated by cross-modal retrieval. Sentence meaning is linearly accessible but highly uneven across languages and resource tiers. Cross-lingual probes can match language-specific probes on languages never seen in probe training, but per-model monolingual decodability does not predict transfer. Within the OmniASR wav2vec family, scaling from 300M--7B disproportionately benefits high-resource languages, and ASR tuning sharply improves semantic decodability while making representations more language-specific. translated_title: 多语言自监督语音编码器对句子意义了解多少？

tldr: 该研究通过将冻结语音表示线性映射到文本嵌入空间并进行跨模态检索，首次大规模评估了自监督语音模型在76种语言中的句子级语义可解码性，发现语义可访问性在语言间高度不均衡、参数扩展偏向高资源语言，且ASR调优虽提升语义可解码性却降低了表示的语言无关性。
